concepts.title: Option contract
concepts.summary: An option gives its holder a contract right; the writer has the corresponding obligation if assigned. Calls and puts express opposite buy or sell rights in the underlying.

concepts.title: Equity options basics
concepts.summary: Standardized equity options specify an underlying, strike, and expiration. Calls and puts create different holder rights and writer obligations; the premium is the option price.

concepts.title: Option premium and pricing drivers
concepts.summary: An option premium is composed of intrinsic value and time value. Underlying price, strike, time to expiration, implied volatility, dividends, and interest rates affect the premium.

concepts.title: Options risk, leverage, and hedging
concepts.summary: Options can hedge an existing position, but all option positions carry risk. A holder can lose the premium paid, while certain uncovered writer positions can have much larger or unlimited loss exposure.

concepts.title: Exercise, assignment, and expiration
concepts.summary: Exercise moves a contract into its delivery obligation, and assignment can be allocated to a short position before expiration. Closing a written option before the market close is the way to avoid assignment for that day.

concepts.title: Delta
concepts.summary: Delta estimates how much an option premium may change for a one-dollar move in the underlying, all else equal. Delta itself changes with moneyness, time to expiration, and implied volatility.

concepts.title: Gamma
concepts.summary: Gamma estimates how Delta may change when the underlying moves. It is generally highest around at-the-money options and closer to expiration, where Delta changes more quickly.

concepts.title: Theta and time decay
concepts.summary: Theta estimates daily option-premium decay with other factors unchanged. Time decay is not linear and tends to accelerate as expiration approaches.

concepts.title: Vega and implied volatility sensitivity
concepts.summary: Vega measures the option premium's sensitivity to a one-percentage-point change in implied volatility. Longer-dated options generally have higher Vega than near-term options.

concepts.title: Option strategy design and payoff principles
concepts.summary: Option strategies can be used to hedge, generate income, or express a directional or neutral view. Risk-defined and uncovered positions differ materially in maximum loss, margin needs, and payoff shape.

strategies.name: Bear Call Spread (Credit Call Spread)
strategies.objective: Collect a net credit when expecting the stock to stay below the short call strike, with upside risk capped by the long call.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral to bearish; does not want the stock above the short call at expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is limited. The best that can happen at expiration is for the stock to be below both strike prices.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited. The worst that can happen at expiration is for the stock price to be above the higher strike.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even at expiration if the stock price is above the lower strike by the amount of the initial credit received. In that case the long call would expire worthless, and the short call's intrinsic value would equal the net credit.
strategies.volatility_effect: Slight, all other things being equal. Since the strategy involves being short one call and long another with the same expiration, the effects of volatility shifts on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time helps the position, though not quite as much as it does a plain short call position. Since the strategy involves being short one call and long another with the same expiration, the effects of time decay on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Yes. Early assignment, while possible at any time, generally occurs when the stock goes ex-dividend. Yes. The investor cannot know for sure whether or not they were assigned on the short call until the Monday after expiration.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For investors seeking premium income with defined maximum loss equal to the width minus credit.

strategies.name: Bear Put Spread
strategies.objective: Express a moderately bearish view with defined risk and reward by offsetting long-put cost with a short lower put.
strategies.market_outlook: Moderately bearish; expects a decline toward or below the short put strike by expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is limited. The best that can happen is for the stock price to be below the lower strike at expiration.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited. The worst that can happen at expiration is for the stock to be above the higher (long put) strike price.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is below the upper strike by the amount of the initial outlay (the debit). In that case, the short put would expire worthless, and the long put's intrinsic value would equal the debit.
strategies.volatility_effect: Slight, all other things being equal. Since the strategy involves being short one put and long another with the same expiration, the effects of volatility shifts on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time hurts the position, though not quite as much as it does an plain long put position. Since the strategy involves being long one put and short another with the same expiration, the effects of time decay on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Yes. Early assignment, while possible at any time, generally occurs only when a put option goes deep into-the-money. Yes. If held into expiration, this strategy entails added risk.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For bearish investors who want defined risk and are willing to cap downside gains.

strategies.name: Bull Call Spread (Debit Call Spread)
strategies.objective: Express a moderately bullish view with defined risk and defined reward by financing a long call with a short higher call.
strategies.market_outlook: Moderately bullish; expects a rise toward or above the short call strike by expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is capped at expiration, should the stock price do even better than hoped and exceed the higher strike price. If the stock price is at or above the higher (short call) strike at expiration, in theory, the investor would exercise the long call component and presumably would be assigned on the short call
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is very limited. The worst that can happen is for the stock to be below the lower strike price at expiration.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even at expiration if the stock price is above the lower strike by the amount of the initial outlay (the debit). In that case, the short call would expire worthless and the long call's intrinsic value would equal the debit.
strategies.volatility_effect: Slight, all other things being equal. Since the strategy involves being long one call and short another with the same expiration, the effects of volatility shifts on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time hurts the position, though not as much as it does a plain long call position. Since the strategy involves being long one call and short another with the same expiration, the effects of time decay on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Early assignment, while possible at any time, generally occurs only when the stock goes ex-dividend. Be warned, however, that using the long call to cover the short call assignment will require establishing a short stock position for one business day, due to the delay in assignment notification. Yes. If held into expiration this strategy entails added risk.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For bullish investors who want lower cost and capped upside versus a naked long call.

strategies.objective: Collect a net credit when expecting the stock to stay above the short put strike, with downside risk capped by the long put.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral to bullish; does not want the stock below the short put at expiration.

strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is below the upper strike (short put strike) by the amount of the initial credit received. In that case, the long put would expire worthless, and the short put's intrinsic value would equal the net credit.
strategies.volatility_effect: Slight, all other things being equal. Since the strategy involves being short one put and long another with the same expiration, the effects of volatility shifts on the two contracts may offset each other to a large degree.

strategies.name: Cash-Secured Put

legs.quantity: one put in the source example
cash equal to strike x 100 shares in the source example

strategies.objective: Acquire stock below the current market price via put assignment, while earning premium if the put expires unassigned.
strategies.market_outlook: Bullish longer term, looking for a short-term dip that may trigger assignment at an acceptable purchase price.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain from the put option itself is limited. However, the optimal outcome is not readily apparent in the expiration profit/loss payoff diagram, because it does not address developments after expiration.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited but substantial. The worst that can happen is for the stock to become worthless.
strategies.breakeven: Since the object of this strategy is to acquire stock, the investor would break even if it is possible to sell the stock at the same effective price they paid for it. Breakeven = strike price – premium
strategies.volatility_effect: Whereas an increase in implied volatility would be considered an unqualified negative for a naked put writer, the effect could be described as neutral to slightly negative for the cash-secured put writer, all other things being equal. If it now appears likelier that the put will be assigned, greater volatility is a neu
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time will have a positive impact on this strategy, all other things being equal. As expiration approaches, the option tends to move toward its intrinsic value, which for out-of-money puts is zero.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Slight. Since the goal of this strategy is to acquire stock, assignment is not a problem. None. Since the goal of this strategy is to acquire stock, the investor should welcome an assignment at the option's expiration.
strategies.suitability_constraints: Only for investors who want to own the stock at the strike (less premium) and have set aside the cash to buy if assigned.

strategies.name: Collar (Protective Collar)
strategies.objective: Temporarily hedge a long stock holding between a put floor and a call ceiling, often at low net premium.
strategies.market_outlook: Wants near-term protection on stock already held; accepts capped upside while the collar is on.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is limited for the term of the strategy. The short-term maximum gains are reached just as the stock price rises to the call strike.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited for the term of the collar hedge. The worst that can happen is for the stock price to fall below the put strike, which prompts the investor to exercise the put and sell the stock at the 'floor' price: the put strike.
strategies.breakeven: In principle, the strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock is above (below) its initial level by the amount of the debit (credit). If the stock is a long-term holding purchased at a much lower price, the concept of breakeven isn't relevant.
strategies.volatility_effect: Volatility is usually not a major consideration in this strategy, all things being equal. Since the strategy involves being long one option and short another with the same expiration (and generally equidistant from the stock value), the effects of implied volatility shifts may offset each other to a large degree.
strategies.time_decay_effect: Usually not a major consideration. Since the strategy involves being long one option and short another with the same expiration (and generally equidistant from the stock value), the effects of time decay should roughly offset each other.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Yes. Early assignment of the short call option, while possible at any time, generally occurs only just before the stock goes ex-dividend. The option writer cannot know for sure whether or not assignment actually occurred on the short call until the following Monday. However, this is generally not an issue since the investor has stock to deliver if assigned on the call.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For stock holders seeking a temporary hedge who accept selling shares at the call strike if assigned.

strategies.name: Covered Call (Buy/Write)

legs.quantity: equivalent amount to the short call; source example uses 100 shares
one call in the source example

strategies.objective: Earn premium income while holding stock, accepting a cap on upside in exchange for a limited downside cushion.
strategies.market_outlook: Steady or slightly rising stock price; not intended for a very bearish or very bullish investor.
strategies.max_gain: Limited. In the source example: strike price minus stock purchase price plus premium received.
strategies.max_loss: Limited but substantial. In the source example: stock purchase price minus premium received; the stock can become worthless.
strategies.breakeven: Starting stock price minus premium received.
strategies.volatility_effect: Neutral to slightly negative when implied volatility rises, all else equal, because buying back the short call can cost more.
strategies.time_decay_effect: Generally positive for the short call position because time erosion reduces the short call's time value, all else equal.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Assignment is central to the strategy; the investor must be willing and able to sell stock at the strike. Early assignment and post-expiration assignment uncertainty require monitoring.
strategies.suitability_constraints: Appropriate only where the investor accepts the preset sale price and can maintain the stock coverage for the short call.

strategies.name: Diagonal Call Spread

legs.quantity: longer-dated call at a different strike

strategies.objective: Combine different strikes and expirations so the payoff differs from a same-strike calendar while still trading time decay.
strategies.market_outlook: Similar to a calendar but strike choice tilts bullish/bearish bias; exact profile depends on selected strikes.
strategies.max_gain: At the expiration of the near-term option, the maximum gain would occur should the underlying stock be at the strike price of the expiring option. If the stock were any higher, the expiring option would have intrinsic value, and if the stock were any lower, the longer-term option would have less value.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss would occur should the two options reach parity. This could happen if the underlying stock declined enough that both options became worthless, or if the stock rose enough that both options went deep in-the-money and traded at their intrinsic value.
strategies.breakeven: Since the options differ in their time to expiration, the level where the strategy breaks even is a function of the underlying stock price, implied volatility and rates of time decay. Should the near-term option expire worthless, breakeven at the longer-term option's expiration would occur if the stock were above the s
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have an extremely positive impact on this strategy. In general, longer-term options have a greater sensitivity to changes in market volatility, i.e., a higher Vega.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, would have a positive impact on this strategy in the beginning. That changes, however, once the near-term option has expired and the strategy becomes simply a long call whose value will be eroded by the passage of time.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Yes. Early assignment, while possible at any time, generally occurs for a call only when the stock goes ex-dividend. Slight. Should the near-term call (the short side of the spread) be exercised when it expires, the longer-term call option would remain to provide a hedge.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For traders who understand both calendar risk and the strike skew of a diagonal; evidence drawn from OIC calendar Variations text.
strategies.review_note: Held at reviewed: OIC has no standalone diagonal page. Definition/legs are supported by calendar Description/Variations, but max_gain/max_loss/breakeven text is still the same-strike calendar profile; publish after a dedicated diagonal source or rewritten fields.

strategies.name: Long Call
strategies.objective: Participate in an expected rise in the underlying with limited risk equal to the premium paid.
strategies.market_outlook: Bullish; wants a timely rally and/or rising implied volatility before expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The profit potential is theoretically unlimited. The best that can happen is for the stock price to rise to infinity.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited and occurs if the investor still holds the call at expiration and the stock is below the strike price. The option would expire worthless, and the loss would be the price paid for the call option.
strategies.breakeven: At expiration, the strategy breaks even if the stock price is equal to the strike price plus the initial cost of the call option. Any stock price above that point produces a net profit.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility would have a positive impact on this strategy, all other things being equal. Volatility tends to boost the value of any long option strategy, because it indicates a greater mathematical probability that the stock will move enough to give the option intrinsic value (or add to its curren
strategies.time_decay_effect: As with most long option strategies, the passage of time has a negative impact here, all other things being equal. As time remaining to expiration disappears, the statistical chances of achieving further gains in intrinsic value shrink.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: None. The investor is in control. Slight. If the option expires in-the-money it may be exercised for you by your brokerage firm.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For bullish investors who accept that the call can expire worthless and that timing before expiration is critical.

strategies.name: Long Call Butterfly

legs.quantity: one upper-strike wing, equidistant, same expiration

strategies.objective: Profit if the underlying finishes near the body strike at expiration, with defined risk equal to the net debit.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / low realized move into expiration around the body.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum profit would occur should the underlying stock be at the middle strike at expiration. In that case, the long call with the lower strike would be in-the-money and all the other options would expire worthless.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss would occur should the underlying stock be outside the wings at expiration. If the stock were below the lower strike all the options would expire worthless; if above the upper strike all the options would be exercised and offset each other for a zero profit.
strategies.breakeven: The strategy breaks even if at expiration the underlying stock is above the lower strike or below the upper strike by the amount of premium paid to initiate the position.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, will usually have a slightly negative impact on this strategy.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, will usually have a positive impact on this strategy if the body of the butterfly is at-the-money, and a negative impact if the body is away from the money.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Yes. The short calls that form the body of the butterfly are subject to exercise at any time, while the investor decides if and when to exercise the wings. Yes. This strategy has an extremely high expiration risk.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For investors seeking defined-risk short-volatility style payoff who accept high expiration pin risk at the body.

strategies.objective: Benefit if the near-term call decays while retaining a longer-dated call; often used with a near-term neutral/bearish and longer-term bullish view.
strategies.market_outlook: Near-term steady or soft, longer-term still constructive; IV changes matter.
strategies.max_gain: At the expiration of the near-term option, the maximum gain would occur should the underlying stock be at the strike price of the expiring option. If the stock were any higher, the expiring option would have intrinsic value, and if the stock were any lower, the longer-term option would have less value.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss would occur should the two options reach parity. This could happen if the underlying stock declined enough that both options became worthless, or if the stock rose enough that both options went deep in-the-money and traded at their intrinsic value.
strategies.breakeven: Since the options differ in their time to expiration, the level where the strategy breaks even is a function of the underlying stock price, implied volatility and rates of time decay. Should the near-term option expire worthless, breakeven at the longer-term option's expiration would occur if the stock were above the s
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have an extremely positive impact on this strategy. In general, longer-term options have a greater sensitivity to changes in market volatility, i.e., a higher Vega.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, would have a positive impact on this strategy in the beginning. That changes, however, once the near-term option has expired and the strategy becomes simply a long call whose value will be eroded by the passage of time.

strategies.suitability_constraints: For traders comfortable managing the front-month expiration and the remaining long call afterward.

strategies.name: Long Call Condor
strategies.objective: Profit if the underlying finishes between the two short strikes, with a wider sweet spot than a butterfly.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / range-bound between the short strikes at expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain would occur if the underlying security is between the two short call strikes at expiration. In that case, the lower strike long call is worth its maximum value.
strategies.max_loss: In all circumstances the maximum loss is limited to the net debit paid (assuming the distances between all four strikes prices are equal). The maximum loss would occur should the underlying be below the lowest long call strike at expiration or at or above the highest long call strike.
strategies.breakeven: There are two breakeven points. This strategy breaks even if at expiration the underlying security is above the lower long call strike plus the amount of premium paid to initiate the position or if the underlying is below the highest long call strike less the premium paid.
strategies.volatility_effect: All other things being equal, an increase in implied volatility if the underlying is between the two short strikes when established would have a negative impact on this strategy. As with most strategies however, the impact of implied volatility changes will depend on strike selection relative to the stock price when th
strategies.time_decay_effect: All other things being equal, the passage of time will have a positive impact on this strategy.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: In the case of American style options, the short options that form the body of the long call condor are subject to assignment at any time. Should early assignment occur on the short call options, the investor can exercise the appropriate long option but may be required to borrow or finance stock for one business day. Investors face an uncertainty when the underlying trades above both short call strikes but below the highest long call strike. In this case, the investor is likely to be assigned on both short calls resulting in a short position that is unhedged following expiration.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For defined-risk traders wanting a wider profit zone than a butterfly, still with multi-leg assignment complexity.

strategies.name: Long Put
strategies.objective: Profit from an expected decline in the underlying with risk limited to the premium paid.
strategies.market_outlook: Bearish; wants a timely drop and/or rising implied volatility before expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The profit potential is limited but substantial. The best that can happen is for the stock to become worthless.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited. The worst that can happen is for the stock price to be above the strike price at expiration with the put owner still holding the position.
strategies.breakeven: At expiration, the strategy breaks even if the stock price equals the strike price minus the cost of the option. Any stock price below that level produces a net profit.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility would have a positive impact on this strategy, all other things being equal. Volatility tends to boost the value of any long option strategy, because it indicates a greater mathematical probability that the stock will move enough to give the option intrinsic value (or add to its curren
strategies.time_decay_effect: As with most long option strategies, the passage of time has a negative impact, all other things being equal. As time remaining until expiration disappears, the statistical chances of achieving further gains shrink.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: None. The investor is in control. Slight. If the option is in-the-money at expiration, it may be exercised on your behalf by your brokerage firm.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For bearish investors who prefer defined risk instead of shorting stock; must realize gains before expiration.

strategies.name: Long Put Condor
strategies.objective: Profit if the underlying finishes between the two short puts at expiration, with defined risk.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / range-bound between the short put strikes at expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain would occur if the underlying security is between the two short put strikes at expiration. In that case, the higher strike long put is worth its maximum value.
strategies.max_loss: In all circumstances the maximum loss is limited to the net debit paid (assuming the distances between all four strikes prices are equal). The maximum loss would occur should the underlying be above the highest long put strike at expiration or at or below the lowest long put strike.
strategies.breakeven: There are two breakeven points. This strategy breaks even if at expiration the underlying security is below the highest long put strike less the amount of premium paid to initiate the position or if the underlying is above the lowest long put strike plus the premium paid.
strategies.volatility_effect: All other things being equal, an increase in implied volatility if the underlying is between the two short strikes when established would have a negative impact on this strategy. As with most strategies however, the impact of implied volatility changes will depend on strike selection relative to the stock price when th
strategies.time_decay_effect: All other things being equal, the passage of time will have a positive effect on this strategy.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: In the case of American style options, the short options that form the body of the long put condor are subject to assignment at any time. Should early assignment occur on the short put options, the investor can exercise the appropriate long option but may be required to borrow or finance stock for one business day. Investors face an uncertainty when the underlying trades below both short put strikes but above the lowest long put strike. In this case, the investor is likely to be assigned on both short puts resulting in a long position that is unhedged following expiration.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For defined-risk traders using puts to express a wide middle sweet spot into expiration.

strategies.name: Long Straddle

legs.quantity: ATM put, same strike and expiration

strategies.objective: Profit from a large move in either direction or a sharp rise in implied volatility.
strategies.market_outlook: Expects a big move up or down; harmed by quiet markets and time decay.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is unlimited. The best that can happen is for the stock to make a big move in either direction.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited to the two premiums paid. The worst that can happen is for the stock price to hold steady and implied volatility to decline.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is either above or below the strike price by the amount of premium paid. At either of those levels, one option's intrinsic value will equal the premium paid for both options while the other option will be expiring worthless.
strategies.volatility_effect: Extremely important. This strategy's success would be fueled by an increase in implied volatility.
strategies.time_decay_effect: Extremely important, negative effect. Because this strategy consists of being long a call and a put, both of them at-the-money at least at the beginning, every day that passes without a move in the stock's price will cause the total premium of this position to suffer a significant erosion of value.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: None. The investor is in control. Slight. If the options are held into expiration, one of them may be subject to automatic exercise.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For investors who can afford two premiums and need a sufficiently large move before expiration.

strategies.name: Long Strangle (Long Combination)
strategies.objective: Profit from a large move either way at lower cost than a straddle, needing a bigger move to break even.
strategies.market_outlook: Expects a large move; quieter than a straddle but still hurt by time decay if the stock stays between strikes.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is unlimited. The maximum gain occurs if the underlying stock goes to infinity, and a very substantial gain would occur if the stock became worthless.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited. The maximum loss occurs if the underlying stock remains between the strike prices until expiration.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is either above the call strike price or below the put strike price by the amount of premium paid. At either of those levels, one option's intrinsic value will equal the premium paid for both options while the other option will be expiring worthless.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have a very positive impact on this strategy. Even if the stock price holds steady, a quick rise in implied volatility would push up the value of both options and might allow the investor to close out the position for a profit well before expiration.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, will have a very negative impact on this strategy. Because the strategy consists of being long two options, every day that passes without a move in the stock's price will cause their value to suffer a significant erosion of value.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: None. The investor is in control. If the options are held into expiration, one of them may be subject to auto-exercise.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For investors seeking cheaper long-volatility exposure who accept a wider breakeven band.

strategies.name: Naked Call (Uncovered Call, Short Call)
strategies.objective: Collect premium income when expecting the underlying to stay flat or fall, accepting theoretically unlimited upside risk.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral to bearish; does not want a sharp rally.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is very limited. The best that can happen is for expiration to arrive with the stock price below the strike price.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is unlimited. The worst that can happen is for the stock to rise to infinity, in which case the investor would have to buy stock in the market at that undefinably high price and sell it at the strike price.
strategies.breakeven: At expiration, the strategy breaks even if the stock price is above the strike price by the amount of the premium received; i.e., the option's intrinsic value equals the price at which the option was sold. Breakeven = strike + premium
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility would have a negative impact on this strategy, all other things equal. It means the market perceives there to be a greater chance than before of the option becoming in-the-money or more in-the-money.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time will have an extremely positive impact on this strategy, all other things equal. As expiration approaches, option values tend to decline toward their intrinsic value.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: There is tremendous assignment risk. Early assignment, while possible at any time, generally occurs only when the stock goes ex-dividend. The option writer cannot know until the Monday following expiration whether or not assignment occurred. And unless the investor is prepared (and approved) to hold a short stock position that is already 'under water' at the strike price, the goal is to buy back the assigned stock as soon as possible.
strategies.suitability_constraints: Only for investors who can post margin and accept theoretically unlimited loss if the stock rises sharply.

strategies.name: Protective Put (Married Put)
strategies.objective: Floor the downside of a long stock position by paying a put premium for temporary protection.
strategies.market_outlook: Bullish or still holding stock, but wants insurance against a near-term decline.
strategies.max_gain: In theory, the potential gains on this strategy are unlimited. The best that can happen is for the stock price to rise to infinity.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is limited. The worst that can happen is for the stock to drop below the strike price.
strategies.breakeven: There is no single formula to determine the strategy's breakeven point. Whether this strategy results in a profit or loss is largely determined by the purchase price of the stock, which may have occurred well in the past at a much lower price.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility would have a neutral to slightly positive impact on this strategy, all other things being equal. On one hand, the investor might perceive a greater value to having the put protection, since the market seems to think a big move has become likely.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time will have a negative impact on this strategy, all other things being equal. The protection of the hedge ends at expiration.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: None. None, providing that the investor knows the pre-established minimum value for automatic exercise. If the protective put holder carries the open position into expiration, it indicates a desire to exercise the option if it's sufficiently in-the-money.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For stock holders willing to pay premium for a known exit floor; not a profit-maximizing income strategy.

strategies.name: Short Iron Butterfly
strategies.objective: Collect credit for a short ATM straddle hedged by a long OTM strangle; profits if price stays near the body.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral; wants the underlying near the body at expiration.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain would occur should the underlying stock be at the body of the butterfly at expiration. In that case all the options would expire worthless, and the premium received to initiate the position could be pocketed.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss would occur should the underlying stock be outside the wings at expiration. In that case either both calls or both puts would be in-the-money.
strategies.breakeven: The strategy breaks even if at expiration the underlying stock is either above or below the body of the butterfly by the amount of premium received to initiate the position.
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have a negative impact on this strategy.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, will have a positive effect on this strategy.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: The short options that form the body of the butterfly are subject to exercise at any time, while the investor decides if and when to exercise the wings. If an early exercise occurs at the body, the investor can choose whether to close out the resulting position in the market or to exercise one of their options (put or  This strategy has expiration risk. If at expiration the stock is trading near the body of the butterfly, the investor faces uncertainty as to whether or not they will be assigned.
strategies.suitability_constraints: For short-premium traders who need defined wings and can handle assignment on the short body options.

strategies.name: Short Condor (Iron Condor)
strategies.objective: Collect credit when expecting the underlying to stay between the short put and short call strikes through expiration.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / range-bound inside the inner wings; rising IV generally hurts.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain would occur should the underlying stock be between the lower call strike and upper put strike at expiration. In that case all the options would expire worthless, and the premium received to initiate the position could be pocketed.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss would occur should the underlying stock be above the upper call strike or below the lower put strike at expiration. In that case either both calls or both puts would be in-the-money.
strategies.breakeven:
This strategy breaks even if at expiration the underlying stock is either above the lower call strike or below the upper put strike by the amount of the premium received to initiate the position. Upside breakeven = lower call strike + premiums received
Downside breakeven = upper put strike - premiums received
strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have a negative impact on this strategy.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, will have a positive effect on this strategy.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: The short options that form the shoulders of the condor's wings are subject to exercise at any time, while the investor decides if and when to exercise the wingtips. strategies.suitability_constraints: For short-premium traders seeking a wider profit zone than an iron butterfly with defined wing risk.

strategies.name: Short Straddle

legs.quantity: ATM put, same strike and expiration

strategies.objective: Collect premium when expecting a narrow trading range and stable or falling implied volatility.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / range-bound; large moves either way are dangerous.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is limited to the premiums received at the outset. The best that can happen is for the stock price, at expiration, to be exactly at the strike price.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum risk is unlimited. The worst that can happen is for the stock to rise to infinity, and the next-to-worst outcome is for the stock to fall to zero.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is either above or below the strike price by the total amount of premium income received. At either of those levels, one option's intrinsic value will equal the premium received for selling both options, while the other option will be expiring worthless.
strategies.volatility_effect: Extremely important. This strategy's chances of success would be better if implied volatility were to fall.
strategies.time_decay_effect: Extremely important positive effect. Every day that passes without a move in the underlying stock price brings both options one day closer to expiring, which would obviously be the investor's best-case scenario.
strategies.assignment_or_expiration_risk: Early assignment, while possible at any time, is more of a risk under certain circumstances: for a call, just before the stock goes ex-dividend; for a put, when it goes deep in-the-money. But the short straddle involves two short legs that could be assigned at any time during the life of the options, so investors shoul The investor cannot know for sure whether or not they were assigned until the Monday after expiration. If the stock hovers just above and below the strike price on the day before expiration, it is even conceivable that both options might be assigned.
strategies.suitability_constraints: Only for investors who can margin short options and accept large or theoretically unlimited risk outside the range.

strategies.name: Short Strangle
strategies.objective: Collect premium with a wider profit zone than a short straddle, still exposed to large moves.
strategies.market_outlook: Neutral / range-bound with room between the short strikes; rising IV hurts.
strategies.max_gain: The maximum gain is very limited. The maximum gain occurs if the underlying stock remains between the strike prices.
strategies.max_loss: The maximum loss is unlimited. The maximum loss occurs if the stock goes to infinity, and a very substantial loss could occur if the stock became worthless.
strategies.breakeven: This strategy breaks even if, at expiration, the stock price is either above the call strike price or below the put strike price by the amount of premium received initially. strategies.volatility_effect: An increase in implied volatility, all other things equal, would have a very negative impact on this strategy. Even if the stock price holds steady, a quick rise in implied volatility would push up the value of both options and force the investor to put up additional margin in order to maintain the position.
strategies.time_decay_effect: The passage of time, all other things equal, will have a very positive impact on this strategy. Every day that passes without a move in the stock price brings both options one day closer to expiring worthless.
